title: Ciudad de México Update — May 16, 2026
summary: One year after the murder of two Clara Brugada government aides at Metro Xola station, authorities confirmed a Tepito-linked criminal cell carried out the killings and reported 18 detentions — with the intellectual author and motive still under investigation. The CNTE teachers' union staged a mega-march through the historic center on Teachers' Day (May 15), blocking Eje 1 Norte and Bucareli en route to the Zócalo. title: Ciudad de México Update — May 09, 2026
summary: Jefa de Gobierno Clara Brugada inaugurated the 'Centro Histórico Iluminado' project — 57 km of renovated corridors, 6,774 streetlights, and 41 historic monuments illuminated for World Cup 2026 — and announced 4,500 new social housing units in the city center. NASA NISAR satellite data published May 5 confirmed Mexico City is sinking up to 14 inches per year at key monitored sites including the AICM airport and Ángel de la Independencia, corroborating earlier UNAM findings. Brugada's constitutional rent-cap reform moved through CDMX Congress committees, and the fifth anniversary of the Metro Line 12 collapse passed with eight of ten charged ex-officials still on trial and zero convictions. May 8 saw eight-plus simultaneous marches including a UNAM student demonstration; BTS drew 50,000 fans to the Zócalo for their 'Arirang' world tour concerts at Estadio GNP (May 7, 9, 10).
